page: Amazon Web Services r7a.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at 3.7 GHz without multithreading contention. It features 16 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. CPU cache hierarchy includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 8 MB L3 cache, backed by vector and cryptographic hardware features including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-threaded CPU capability, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the top quartile. However, overall multi-threaded throughput is bounded by the dual-core profile, with PassMark CPU, compilation tasks, and multi-core Geekbench scores placing in lower tiers. Memory tests show uncached large-block read speeds of 36.7 GB/s and write speeds of 27.09 GB/s, alongside a PassMark memory score in the middle range.

The r7a.large does not include bundled local storage or discrete graphics accelerators, depending exclusively on networked storage services over a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. From a resource-density perspective, it offers a cost-effective path to modern DDR5 capacity for applications needing substantial RAM per core without incurring the expense of unneeded compute capacity.

Amazon Web Services r7a.large is appropriate for small-footprint in-memory caches, lightweight relational or key-value databases, background task queues, and microservices requiring high memory density alongside solid single-thread performance.
